scientific_question: With known fault truth held constant in both arms, does a known-delivered nonzero native rotation probe change required full-SE3 target-anchor repair, and does an intervention-aware inverse restore the t1 anchor better than a counterfactual no-probe inverse?
claim_boundary: This isolates intervention semantics under oracle-known fault truth. It is NOT passive ACK identification, not trained policy or task success, not a safe RL certificate, not independent adoption.
fixed_anchor: controller target full position/quaternion after common known-delivered t0,t1; repair attempts restoration of EXACT fixed t1 target, unlike earlier moving held target reference
source_actions: same existing research/cross_robot_ack_physics.py native t0/t1/t2, with held t2 physically sent zero, applied t2 physically sent source t2
strict_matching: two repair comparators physically rerun identical reset/ACK/probe t0:t3 action prefix; audit actual command target after t1, t3 and t4
truth_as_decision_input: both inverse comparators get oracle physical ACK truth for controlled repair-semantic ablation; no ACK detection algorithm and no private getter pre-repair inputs
posthoc_private_target_reads: allowed only for audit of predicted target and final physically executed restoration, never passed into inverse controller
primary_outcomes: same-prefix physically achieved EE displacement before repair
known-delivered rotation probe real target SO3 change
static vs dynamic full-SE3 commanded target restoration per paired seed/truth/probe
actual t4 task success recorded ONLY as context and never interpreted as manipulation-task success if initial task was not completed
all 128 worlds completed with source checksum provenance
hard_vetoes: do not posthoc choose different probes, seeds or action amplitudes
do not relabel task-level success from SE3 commanded target restoration
do not count correlated truth/probe/repair worlds as independent seeds
do not claim nonzero active information gain: fault truth supplied by oracle to both controllers
the anchor fixed at t1 changes the repair objective relative to prior moving-target experiments
do not claim general hardware safety or read atomicity from an author-operated scripted PhysX test
